title: Opinion polls (party vote) for the 2026 New Zealand general election, since the 14 Oct 2023 election
notes: Percentages as published (decided voters; undecided excluded by every pollster). 'end_date' is the sort date used by Wikipedia (last fieldwork day or release date). Rows are newest first. 'others' = combined minor parties where listed. 'pollster_key' groups series that changed name; 'internal' marks party/corporate-client polls that are published selectively. Poll sources: each row's source_url as linked on Wikipedia. Refreshed by tools/polls_update.py.

events.event: Advance voting begins for the 2026 New Zealand general election .
Tāmaki Makaurau electorate candidate Kerrin Leoni resigns from the Labour Party.
Prime Minister and National Party leader Christopher Luxon survives a second party leadership vote .
Budget 2026 is delivered.
Mariameno Kapa-Kingi exits Te Pāti Māori to start Te Tai Tokerau Party .
Prime Minister and National Party leader Christopher Luxon survives a party leadership vote called by himself.
The Strait of Hormuz is closed as part of the Iran war , causing an incoming fuel crisis affecting New Zealand.
Prime Minister Christopher Luxon announces that the election will be held on 7 November 2026.
Mariameno Kapa-Kingi reinstated as a member of Te Pāti Māori by the High Court.
Qiulae Wong becomes leader of The Opportunity Party .
Tākuta Ferris and Mariameno Kapa-Kingi are expelled from Te Pāti Māori.
Oriini Kaipara of Te Pāti Māori wins the Tāmaki Makaurau by-election .
David Seymour of the ACT party becomes Deputy Prime Minister, replacing Winston Peters of NZ First.
Budget 2025 is delivered.
Hīkoi mō te Tiriti protest against the Treaty Principles Bill .
Budget 2024 is delivered.
Chlöe Swarbrick is elected as co-leader of the Green Party .
James Shaw announces his intention to resign as co-leader of the Green Party in March 2024.
Raf Manji resigns as leader of The Opportunities Party .
Christopher Luxon is sworn in as Prime Minister of New Zealand .

1 News–Verian.method: Landline + mobile CATI and online panel, n≈1,000, max. sampling error ±3.1 pts at 95%

Taxpayers' Union–Curia.method: Phone + online panel, n≈1,000, ±3.1 pts; Curia left RANZ in 2024

Roy Morgan.method: Telephone/online, fieldwork spans the whole month, n≈800–1,000

Talbot Mills.commissioner: Talbot Mills Research (corporate-client poll; also Labour's pollster, formerly UMR)
Talbot Mills.method: Online panel, n≈1,000; results leaked/published irregularly

Anacta.commissioner: Anacta Consulting (corporate clients; has polled for Labour)
Anacta.method: Online, n≈1,300–1,700; published via NZ Herald / The Post

Curia.commissioner: Curia Market Research (National's pollster) - publicly released polls not sponsored by the Taxpayers' Union

electorate_polls_note: Electorate-level polls from the same Wikipedia article (section 'Electorate polling'). 'vote' = party or electorate (candidate) vote. Small samples (n≈400–800); treat as indicative only.
